title: Record the declared model for herding and cli dispatches, from both writers
action:
Read plan.md revision 2 first; it defines every case below.

1. **The helper.** In `packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/models.rs`, beside `resolve_role`:
```rust
/// leader-sees-team D2: the model an external program was ASKED for, read from the argv bee built.
pub(crate) fn declared_model_for(cfg: &Value, resolved: &Resolved, runtime: &str) -> Option<String>
```
- `Resolved::Herding { agent, .. }` (BOTH arms — `agent: None` too): resolve the argv with `crate::herding::wave::resolve_agent_command_for_runtime(cfg, agent.as_deref(), runtime)` and scan its args.
- `Resolved::Cli { command }`: split the command string quote-aware (a small tokenizer; single and double quotes), then scan.
- Anything else → `None`.
- Scan rule: accept `--model X`, `--model=X`, `-m X`. If more than one is present, the FIRST wins — record this as a named guess in the doc comment.

2. **The sixth argument.** `derive_economics` in `verbs/drivers/guard.rs:342` gains `declared: Option<&str>`. When `channel` is `herding-exec` or `cli-exec` and `declared` is `Some(m)`: `requested_model = m`, `effective_model_status = "declared"`. When `None`: today's exact bytes (`null`, `"unverified"`) — the test at `guard.rs:670` must still pass unchanged. `effective_model` stays null in both cases. Every other channel is untouched. Update the five existing test call sites (`guard.rs:667,676`, `tests.rs:748,755,769,776,782`) to pass `None`.

3. **The caller.** In `verbs/drivers/prepare.rs` beside `param_model` (`:1972-1975`), compute `let declared = declared_model_for(&cfg, &resolved, runtime)` for BOTH cli-exec sites (`:1755` and `:1781`) and the herding-exec site. At the `:1755` site `resolved` is a `Resolved::Native` whose fallback COMMAND runs — read that command string, never the Native `model` field. Pass `declared.as_deref()` at `:1979`. A herding `fallback` model (`:1870-1887`) is untouched; the record describes the primary argv only.

4. **The second writer.** `hooks/model_guard.rs` `derive_dispatch_economics` (`:1213-1258`) recomputes the six fields itself and maps `Resolved::Herding` to no model (`resolved_model_name`, `:331-335`). Make it call the same helper for a `Herding` or `Cli` resolution so its audit row carries the same `requested_model`/`declared` prepare's row would. It has `models` (the team subtree) — give it the whole config it needs.

5. **Tests** (in `guard.rs` / `models.rs` / `model_guard.rs` test modules, whichever owns the code): `--model X` → declared; `--model=X` → declared; `-m X` → declared; two tokens → first; `agent: None` resolving through the generation slot; a fixture registry entry with NO model token → exactly claim-10 bytes; `Native` on cli-exec → the fallback command's model, never the model field; native model slot still `pinned`; session-model still `inherited-or-unknown`; and one test asserting prepare's row and the guard's row agree for a herding slot.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- drivers model_guard
